description.short_caption: Chest CT showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung abnormalities. There is a diffuse, reticular pattern with areas of ground-glass opacities and interstitial thickening, predominantly in the lower lung zones. The mediastinum appears central, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The findings are suggestive of a diffuse interstitial process.
visible_findings: bilateral reticular pattern in the lungs

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung involvement with patchy areas of ground-glass opacities and consolidation, predominantly in the lower lobes. The findings suggest a diffuse inflammatory or infectious process. The mediastinum and bony structures appear unremarkable. No contrast enhancement is evident, indicating a non-contrast study.

description.short_caption: Cytopathology of BAL showing fungal elements with budding yeast forms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a cytopathology preparation from a bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) sample stained with a fungal stain (likely GMS or PAS). Numerous round to oval yeast forms are visible, some of which exhibit budding. The background contains cellular debris and scattered inflammatory cells. A large, darkly stained nucleus of a host cell is also prominent in the field. The findings are consistent with a fungal infection, potentially involving a yeast species.
visible_findings: background of cellular debris and inflammatory cells
